purpose: Semantic alignment for reuse; not an official AIID submission schema or OECD AIM ingest schema.

status_definitions.direct: AAIO captures the same concept closely enough to transfer without semantic inference.
status_definitions.partial: AAIO captures only part of the target concept or lacks required subfields.
status_definitions.approximate: AAIO captures related information, but semantics or controlled vocabularies differ.
status_definitions.unmapped: AAIO does not currently capture the target concept in a defensible structured field.
status_definitions.cross_reference_only: AAIO stores an external identifier or URL but does not reproduce the external record schema.

aiid_core.note: Populated only when AAIO has already matched the event to an existing AIID incident.
AAIO title is neutral and concise, but it is not claimed to be AIID editor-approved wording.
AAIO summary is source-calibrated and preserved verbatim in the interoperability export.
AAIO records the earliest reasonably supported date and separately preserves its precision.
AAIO v0.1.0 does not maintain normalized developer entity roles.
AAIO v0.1.0 does not maintain normalized deployer entity roles.
AAIO affected_parties is broader than AIID's normalized harmed/nearly harmed entity model and is exported only as candidate labels.
AAIO preserves source names, URLs and source types but not the complete metadata of an AIID report object.
AIID supports multiple independent taxonomies. AAIO does not manufacture CSET, GMF, MIT or other taxonomy annotations.

oecd_common_reporting_framework.name: How is the AI system(s) related to the incident
Name and version of the AI system(s)/product(s)
Organisation(s) that developed and/or deployed the AI system
Severity
oecd_common_reporting_framework.note: AAIO's project severity rubric is not equivalent to OECD CRF severity categories and is never converted automatically.

oecd_common_reporting_framework.name: Harm type
oecd_common_reporting_framework.note: AAIO harm descriptors are free-form project labels, not OECD controlled values.

oecd_common_reporting_framework.name: Incident linked to use of AI system(s) in unintended/wrongful way
oecd_common_reporting_framework.note: Reported intent is not equivalent to the OECD wrongful-use criterion.

oecd_common_reporting_framework.name: Affected stakeholder(s)
oecd_common_reporting_framework.note: AAIO labels are preserved but not silently converted to OECD stakeholder categories.

oecd_common_reporting_framework.name: Adverse impacts on human rights or fundamental rights
Industry(ies)
oecd_common_reporting_framework.note: AAIO sector labels are not ISIC-coded.

oecd_common_reporting_framework.name: Business function(s) where the AI incident occurred
Incident linked to the functioning of critical functions/infrastructure
Breadth of deployment
oecd_common_reporting_framework.note: AAIO scale is an impact dimension and must not be reused as deployment breadth.

oecd_common_reporting_framework.name: Incident linked to the training data of AI system(s)
Incident linked to the AI model
Incident linked to interaction of multiple AI systems
Task(s) of AI system(s)
oecd_common_reporting_framework.note: AAIO system_type is descriptive and is not converted to OECD task categories without manual review.

oecd_common_reporting_framework.name: Maximum autonomy level of AI system(s)
Action(s) taken
oecd_common_reporting_framework.note: AAIO response is free text and is not automatically converted to OECD action categories.
